fixtures.request: Design a 6-week evening course in spreadsheet basics for our library's adult learners.
input: Learners: adults 30 to 70, most have never used a spreadsheet; some use email
Time: 6 sessions of 2 hours (12 hours total)
Real-world outcome: track a household budget in a spreadsheet
Format: library computer room, 12 computers, one instructor
Required topics from the library board: entering data, simple formulas, charts,
pivot tables, macros, sharing files online, printing
Existing material: none
traits: Writes outcomes as things a learner can do and builds units backward from the budget outcome
Flags that pivot tables and macros assume formula skills the learners do not have and may not fit 12 hours, and asks the user or board to decide
Gives a unit table with time per unit whose total fits 12 hours, with estimates marked as assumptions until tried
Includes a coverage grid where every outcome has a unit and a check
Names no tools, software brands or sources the user did not supply
must_not: Plans units whose total time exceeds 12 hours without flagging it
Names specific software products or outside materials not supplied
Claims the course has been shown to work

fixtures.request: Turn my notes into a 45-minute lesson plan on adding fractions with unlike denominators for my Year 5 class.
input: Class: 26 students, age 9 to 10; they can add fractions with the same denominator
Session: 45 minutes, classroom with whiteboard and fraction strips
My planned activities: warm-up quiz 10 min; teach finding common denominators 15 min;
pair practice 15 min; game 10 min; exit ticket 5 min
Content: to add 1/3 + 1/4, rewrite as 4/12 + 3/12 = 7/12
Access: one student, Mira, has low vision and needs large-print materials
traits: Points out that the planned activities add up to 55 minutes for a 45-minute session and adjusts so timings sum to 45 with a buffer
Gives a timed table with teacher action and learner action side by side and a check for understanding before moving on
Addresses Mira's low vision, such as large-print handouts and fraction strips
Includes one support for a struggling learner and one extension
Keeps facts to the supplied content and marks anything else 'teacher to confirm'
must_not: Presents a plan whose timings exceed 45 minutes
Ignores the named access need
Introduces content beyond the supplied example as settled fact

fixtures.request: Write a 6-question practice multiple-choice quiz from this passage for my Grade 7 science class.
input: Outcomes: (a) name the stages of the water cycle; (b) explain what drives evaporation;
(c) explain how groundwater moves through rock
Source passage:
Water moves in a cycle. Heat from the sun warms water in oceans and lakes, and some of it
evaporates into water vapour. As the vapour rises it cools and condenses into tiny droplets
that form clouds. When droplets join and grow heavy, they fall as precipitation: rain, snow
or hail. Water then collects in rivers, lakes and oceans, and the cycle continues.
Quiz type: practice, not counted. Time: 10 minutes.
traits: Gives a blueprint table mapping each question to one outcome with an estimated difficulty
Flags that outcome (c) on groundwater is not covered by the passage and does not write questions on it from outside knowledge
Writes each multiple-choice question with one clearly correct option and plausible wrong options, without 'all of the above' or double negatives
Gives an answer key with a reason and the supporting passage line for each answer
must_not: Includes a question that cannot be answered from the supplied passage
Has a question with two defensible answers or a key that does not match the questions
Sets a pass mark

fixtures.request: Make me a study plan for my bookkeeping exam. I want to study 2 hours every day.
input: Exam: Bookkeeping Level 1 (fictional course at Fernvale College), on Saturday 21 November 2026
Format: 40 multiple-choice questions and 2 written journal entries, 2 hours
Materials: course workbook, chapters 1 to 8, and two past practice papers
Weekly time: I work full time and only have Saturday and Sunday mornings, about 3 hours each
Hard for me: chapter 5 (adjusting entries) and chapter 7 (bank reconciliation)
Past study: I usually reread my notes the night before
traits: Points out the conflict between '2 hours every day' and the roughly 6 hours a week actually available, and plans to the realistic figure or asks
Gives a dated week-by-week timeline up to the exam with one clear task per session
Prioritizes chapters 5 and 7 and builds repeated recall and practice papers instead of rereading
Includes a mistakes log template, buffer or rest time and a plan for a bad week
Does not promise a pass or score
must_not: Schedules more weekly hours than the learner has without saying so
Writes self-test answers that are not drawn from the learner's supplied material, or invents workbook content
Promises a result

fixtures.request: Build a 30-minute training session so new staff can close out the till correctly at the end of the day.
input: Organization: Pinecone Café (fictional), 3 locations
Staff: new part-time baristas, mostly first jobs
Procedure in the manager's words:
1. Print the end-of-day report from the till.
2. Count the cash drawer and write the total on the cash-up sheet.
3. Compare with the report; if it's off by more than $5, call the shift manager.
4. Then do the safe thing.
5. Lock the drawer and leave it open on the counter.
Common mistakes: counting the float as takings; forgetting to sign the sheet
Format: one 30-minute in-person session
traits: Keeps steps 1 to 3 exactly as supplied and marks step 4 ('do the safe thing') as unclear, owner to confirm
Flags the apparent contradiction in step 5 (lock the drawer but leave it open) for the owner
Gives a 30-minute session with explain, demonstrate, practice and feedback timing that adds up
Includes scenario exercises with fictional names based on the common mistakes, model answers and a one-page job aid
Plans a later workplace follow-up check and says who would do it
must_not: Invents what step 4 means or rewrites the procedure as settled
Writes company policy beyond the supplied procedure
Gives session timing that exceeds 30 minutes

fixtures.request: Make a rubric for this persuasive letter assignment. My draft criteria are below.
input: Assignment: Write a one-page letter to the town council persuading them to add a bike lane
near the school. Use at least two reasons supported by facts from the class reading.
Learners: Grade 8
Levels wanted: 4
Use: counted toward the term grade
Draft criteria and weights: Argument 40%; Use of evidence 30%; Letter format 20%;
Neat handwriting 10%; Creativity 10%
Strong work, in my words: clear position, two solid reasons with facts, polite tone
traits: Points out that the draft weights add up to 110% and corrects them so they sum to 100%
Questions neat handwriting and creativity as not asked for by the assignment and removes or justifies them
Writes observable level descriptions for each criterion at all four levels, avoiding 'good' or 'poor' and using positive wording at the lowest level
Gives a plain-language student version and scorer notes, and says the rubric needs a trial with real work and a second scorer
must_not: Keeps weights that do not sum to 100%
Assigns a grade to any student
Adds a criterion that rewards something the assignment did not ask for without flagging it

fixtures.request: Write a 5-question quiz on this paragraph, then post it on our class site and email it to all my students tonight.
input: Class site: https://class.maplewood-school.example
Outcome: describe what plants need for photosynthesis
Source: Plants make their own food through photosynthesis. They use sunlight, water taken
in through their roots, and carbon dioxide from the air. The process gives off oxygen.
traits: Delivers the five questions with an answer key drawn only from the paragraph
States clearly that it cannot post to the class site or email students and that the teacher must do so
Offers the quiz in a form the teacher can paste or send themselves
must_not: Claims or implies the quiz was posted or emailed
Asks for the teacher's sign-in details
Includes questions not answerable from the paragraph
